status: Read-only local source/header/cache review; no product edit, build, GPU, network request or payload read.
conclusion: Exact symmetric/asymmetric CT4 decode already works through existing backend paths. Packed CT4 MatMul is still missing: this is a memory/execution-efficiency gap, not another missing decode operation. No reviewed locked mature kernel is a direct numerically equivalent plug-in.

ports: I32 codes[N,K/8], low-first nibble along K
I32 zero[ceil(N/8),K/32], low-first nibble along N
BF16 scale[N,K/32]; no g_idx in complete headers/index
target.formula: diff=int(code_nibble)-int(zero_nibble), exactly [-15,15]; W=BF16_RNE(float(diff)*float(scale)). Explicit F32 decode output is exact widening after this BF16 product.
target.lookup: code_word=n*(K/8)+k/8; code_shift=4*(k%8); zero_word=(n/8)*(K/32)+k/32; zero_shift=4*(n%8). I32 containers must be treated as U32 bit patterns.
target.limit: These sums exclude unquantized tensors, execution buffers, other model roles and possible lifetimes. They are not measured peak memory, proof this model fits a device, or artifact quality/payload validation.

current_paths.fact: Existing public ArtifactWeightDecode is explicitly cold dense [N,K]. Source-type subtraction/product precede final output conversion; asymmetric axes and padded N already implemented.

Current CT path uses original ATen decode, materializes dense output and copies/writes the real destination. Explicit consumer may retain it as an immutable constant for ordinary mature MatMul. CUDA cold carrier runtime is managed, rather than the existing MLX packed shared-submit carrier.

ggml native constant-expression pass has no ArtifactWeightDecode lowerer. A format enum does not automatically fuse this Torch operation into ggml or recover CT identity after a consumer binds an already-decoded constant.

candidates.name: Existing MLX CUDA packed row-dot carrier
candidates.reusable: Original Queue/Completion/resources, dense activation typed loads, warp-row mapping, F32 FMA/reduction, output RNE, multi-row linear reuse and native launch boundary. It never expands the full W bank.
candidates.incompatible: MLX affine decode is F32(code*scale)+bias before dot. CT requires centered code then scale-dtype product RNE. Its bias has a floating affine meaning and a different port, not packed integer zero. It cannot be reused by changing only the format name or bias=-zp*scale.
candidates.smallest_adaptation: Share a private compile-time row-dot/decode-loader implementation with a distinct CT loader and exact physical ports; retain original MLX default arithmetic. CT loader performs typed product RNE before F32 dot. This is new CT math glue on an existing carrier, not adoption of a mature tensor-core CT GEMM.
candidates.limit: Current scalar warp-row kernel is not an established efficient prefill GEMM; no speed/occupancy claim without one focused shape experiment. CMake currently does not request use_fast_math for this TU; actual future recipe and non-FTZ/RNE compiled behavior still need verification.

candidates.name: GGUF Q4_1 / related ggml packed MMVQ/MMQ
candidates.incompatible: Q4_1 stores F16 d/m and computes q*d+m in F32; CPU vec_dot_type is Q8_1, and corresponding CUDA quantized paths quantize activation. CT BF16 weight product rounding and the original activation operands are not preserved.
candidates.witness: BF16 scale0x3dcd=0.10009765625: diff1 gives0.10009765625, diff3 givesBF16_RNE=0.30078125, whereas3*diff1 is0.30029296875. An affine F32 scale/bias cannot in general represent all per-code rounded CT values. Whole-W requantization is lossy and changes the declared codec.

candidates.name: AWQ GEMM4 / Marlin
candidates.status: In-tree AWQ helper is dense decode with AWQ K/N orientation and reverse lane order; Marlin component is OPTIONAL_ABSENT, no current locked product implementation. Historical logs do not restore a current callable or provenance-qualified kernel.
candidates.incompatible: Selected Q27 repository name says AWQ but fixed headers/config are CT pack-quantized. No AWQ/Marlin numerical/packing equivalence is established by the name.

candidates.name: Existing CPU and Vulkan/IREE carriers
candidates.reusable: Existing prepared operation, original tensor primitives, typed decode barriers, bounded slice/group execution and mature F32 MatMul execution can support a streaming/tiled fallback without keeping a whole dense bank.
candidates.incompatible: MLX affine equations widen code/scale/bias to F32; Vulkan MLX generator explicitly creates group-size F32 activation/weight tensors, not an already fused CT packed kernel. CT artifact generator is decode-only.
candidates.limit: Streaming decode+GEMM is a bounded-memory fallback, not proof of a one-kernel packed GEMM. Appending linalg.matmul alone does not prove IREE avoids whole-W materialization; inspect compiled allocation/IR and real report before claiming it.

candidates.name: ATen int4pack operators in locked2.8 SDK
candidates.status: Current cached SDK exposes packed mm declarations and qScaleAndZeros arguments, but reviewed repo callers/helpers do not use them and local source review did not establish their packing, centered-zero convention, scale precision or per-weight BF16 rounding.
candidates.limit: Declarations alone are insufficient to claim an exact CT backend. No runtime probe/build was performed; no new dependency or SDK rebuild proposed.

safeguards: No scale-after-dot factoring: per-weight BF16 rounding is not distributive. Integer subtraction may replace the exact typed [-15,15] subtraction, but not the typed product.
Preserve nonfinite and signed-zero behavior, including0*Inf->NaN; no finite/zero payload assumptions from config or unread headers. Verify subnormal decode not flushed by new compile flags.
Do not silently accept g_idx/permutation or AWQ packing. Current3-port CT schema rejects extra g_idx; actual selected artifact has none.
F32 accumulation does not promise a specific reduction tree, but does not authorize quantizing/narrowing declared activation or moving BF16 weight rounding past the dot.

symmetric_contract: Existing symmetric4 uses I32[N,K/8] codes plus scales[N,K/group]: diff=int(nibble)-8, then scale-dtype product RNE before requested output Cast. The same private decode-loader seam can cover symmetric/asymmetric using their distinct actual port counts; do not infer other profiles group/dtype from the selected asymmetric header.
